voice: A dignified and forceful eyewitness who demands justice for the dead, retaining restrained religious conviction without pulp-Egyptian insults or desert cliches.

entries.text: I have one final piece of evidence to present, Mr. Coroner. An eyewitness would only come forward if I established my case against Mr. O'Riley. Now that I have, allow me to introduce Dr. Ptahsheptut Smith of the Cairo Museum.
Dr. Smith, your testimony will be protected.

Thank you. I was in the Egyptian ceremonial chamber beneath the museum when Detective O'Riley killed two members of our society. I saw him shoot them without mercy when they tried to stop him from pursuing Miss Bow.
We delayed him, but we could not stop him. His hood slipped back as he fired, and I saw his face clearly. That man must not be allowed to escape justice.
Will you testify in court to what you witnessed, Dr. Smith?
I will. My dead companions deserve justice. O'Riley may answer to your court in this life; Amon Ra may judge what remains.
The disposition of his spirit is beyond my office, Dr. Smith, but your testimony will help us answer for the dead. Thank you for coming forward.
